newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Industrivarden says buys Sandvik shares at 185 SKR.
newsitem.headline: Industrivarden says buys Sandvik shares at 185 SKR.

text.p: Swedish investment company Industrivarden said on Monday that it was buying 22 million A-shares in engineer Sandvik at a price of 185 crowns each worth with total investment of 4.1 billion crowns.
On Friday Sandvik shares closed at 193.5 crowns.
Industrivarden is buying the stake from construction group Skanska which announced on Monday it was selling its entire stake in Sandvik.
The price of 185 crowns a share excluded the proposed 1996 dividend.

Industrivarden said Sandvik's strategy was to increase growth and optimise capital structure. Sandvik is also seen having large market share in Europe with good possibility of growth in the rest of the world. Sandvik has introduced products with large potential, according to Industrivarden.
"Industrivarden thinks the market evaluation of the Sandvik share does not fully reflect the company's possibilities in the future," Industrivarden said in a statement.
Industrivarden said it aims to be an active owner in Sandvik and contribute to the company's development.
"The strategy of Industrivarden is to invest in shares which in the long run will exceed the bourse index," Industrivarden writes. Industrivarden is financing the purchase through borrowing.
